analysis.title: GS McGeoch - GS Materials Nov 24...meh....Rally fade, Copper short (total commod short), BHP's jenga set, GLEN coal breakout, NHY CMD tomorrow....RWE
key_insights: McGeoch expects a softer start. The recent commodity pop was short covering, with SHFE copper open interest up c.30% even as longs were cut. Active players are buying puts and delta hedging adds downside pressure.

Demand is described as still very average absent policy support. Desk looks for a catalyst such as oil at $70, DXY below 100 or 98, or yields at 4.5%. Risk appetite is low and copper technicals remain a fade for CTAs.

Copper demand framing: AI is under 2% of copper demand and electrification/transmission is c.45%. Grid spend is a waiting game on trade and policy. McGeoch is painfully holding copper longs and disagrees with the desk that copper is the better rally to sell.

Drawdowns from highs: Cu -25%, Zinc -16%, Ali -33%, Ni -28%. He thinks it is too early to talk of a $13k target because few believe the supply issue matters in 2027 and tariffs remain a risk with easy re-exporting of tonnes.

Chinese shorts on LME added c.24k lot equivalents from a base of c.14,500, roughly a 28% increase. Shorts rose in iron ore, rebar, China NRC and coking coal, while longs fell in Ali, Zinc and Copper per CFTC data.
Expects SXPP to start down 1-2%. SXPP was +3.5% yesterday, -7.5% MTD, +3% YTD and -25% post summer. Lutnick testimony on Dec 10 is flagged as a policy target.

US tape: ETFs were c.37% of volume, the highest since April versus a 5yr avg of 25%. Levered ETFs were about $1 of every $4 of ETF volume, a record share. ETF short flows rose 8.5% Friday and 19% last week, the 3rd largest weekly rise in a decade.
Liquidity is thin. S&P 500 top of book is around $2mm versus a 5yr avg of $11mm, an intraday YTD low, which exacerbates price moves.

Oil: the late move lower had no clear catalyst and looks near-term overextended. Brent front month is through the Nov 10 lows, Dubai physical is at a discount to prompt for the first time since June, and DXY is at resistance. The desk would still fade rallies and prefers long commodity over equities, with BP as an interesting relative long.

Var Energi / Conoco Norway deal pro-forma: adds c.115 kboe/d, 414 mmboe 2P, and takes pro-forma 2026 production to c.550 kboe/d. GS estimates +16% to +25% accretion to 2028E CFFO/share and +15% to +66% to FCF/share, lower with a 10% equity raise.
Vallourec rated Buy with PT EUR26.90, c.80% upside. The post-results sell-off is seen as an opportunity and the valuation gap to Tenaris is expected to narrow.

BHP copper trip: admitted capital inflation of 8% pa, block cave construction and capex escalation are the key asks. Capex is expected to drift and sit around 3rd/4th quartile. Copper production is 2mt today, not back to that until FY23 per the note, peaking +10% in FY35. Kokatha native title compensation talks add pressure.

GLEN coal breakout: Newcastle coal in AUD made a new high. BHP is +20% YTD TR versus GLEN +14%. GLEN trades below 0.5x the multiple with almost 3x the FCF yield and the same dividend yield, with a buyback.
First Quantum is targeting a 1Q27 outcome with the Panama government on the copper mine.

Norsk Hydro CMD Wednesday 9am with pre-market release expected. Buyside leans to NOK14bn capex versus consensus 14.2bn. McGeoch sees commodity price as the main driver, volume recovery from Q2 onwards, and sees better value elsewhere. NHY YTD TR is -14.5%.

RWE March 2027 CMD preview: GS expects guidance extended to 2032, earnings nearly doubling over 2027-32 (+13% CAGR), c.EUR45bn consolidated capex (c.EUR80bn incl. equity accounted), c.35% of profits from grids, and P/E of 9x by 2032.
